*Finance SC Minutes*

August 11, 2026
City Council Chamber / Zoom
5:30 PM

### PRESENT:

Present on Roll Call were C. Juran and C. McDonough, 1 absent (C. Scott). Also present Conor Baldwin (CFO); Terry Ryan (Parking Dir.); and Austin Ball (Asst. CFO).

### MEETING CALLED TO ORDER:

C. Juran called the meeting to order noting those in attendance and agenda items which she noted will be taken out of order.

### ORDER OF BUSINESS:

Mr. Baldwin provided presentation entitled "Finance Subcommittee Meeting – August 11, 2026". C. Juran requested presentation be added to minutes of this meeting. (See Attached) Mr. Baldwin noted three items on the agenda; wages; budget stressors; and parking fees. Mr. Baldwin opened discussion with budget stressors indicating they include fixed costs, health costs and debt service. Mr. Baldwin noted in regard to the fixed costs the charter school costs that they are a Cherry Sheet allotment and they rise annually. Mr. Baldwin noted that the City applies pressure each year to the legislature to change formula to lessen the burden on local municipalities. C. Juran questioned the reimbursement formula and how it could be changed. C. McDonough questioned the status of charter schools in the City. Mr. Baldwin noted the increase in costs and that any costs are a part of Net School Spending. C. McDonough commented that charter schools should have to pay for costs that public schools are required to pay. Mr. Baldwin noted that there are some overlaps in services.

The second item discussed by Mr. Baldwin was health costs. Mr. Baldwin noted City was a part of the state GIC program. Mr. Baldwin noted at the outset of the program there were good savings, but they have diminished over the years. Mr. Baldwin noted that the coverage is for city and school employees. Mr. Baldwin indicated that there has been some research regarding going to a private vendor for these services. C. Juran noted GIC coverage is the same for all municipalities. Mr. Baldwin noted the only changes are as to the scale of coverage. C. McDonough suggested a per costs for employees could be used to reduce costs within the GIC. Mr. Baldwin indicated that there has been some discussion regarding "buy out" costs.

The next agenda item reviewed by Mr. Baldwin regarded pension costs. Mr. Baldwin noted they were part of the state system which oversee the investments. Mr. Baldwin noted date in which City must fully fund the system but indicated there are ways to extend that date. Mr. Baldwin noted that teachers are under a different retirement system. C. McDonough noted that paraprofessionals in the classroom should be under the same system of the teachers.

Mr. Baldwin commented on current debt service of the City. Mr. Baldwin noted the largest debt involves the school buildings, driven by the high school and the many MSBA projects. Mr. Baldwin noted the debt service has grown due to the number of investments in the City. Mr. Baldwin noted that debt could decrease if not all funding is used or if there were a more favorable reimbursement rate by the MSBA. Mr. Baldwin outlined current debt and what future debt will be taken on by the City. Mr. Baldwin noted if debt is managed properly, it derives many benefits.

The last budget stressor discussed was energy costs. Mr. Baldwin noted the yearly increases and the many programs used to reduce those increases. In conclusion Mr. Baldwin indicated that the administration would continue to work with delegation to benefit the City.

The second item on agenda for discussion was parking fees. Mr. Baldwin commented how the fees are tied to a price index and that there is a need for an escalator clause to keep Parking Enterprise Fund viable, outlining the costs without increased rates. Mr. Baldwin outlined the differences between transient parking and pass holders, noting that big institutions are not included with the pass holders. C. McDonough questioned the student rates and that they may need to be increased. C. Juran commented on costs at the LRTA facility. C. Juran noted more research would be needed to fully develop the program. C. McDonough noted adjustments to certain rates may cover any potential costs.

C. Juran noted upcoming Finance SC on September 8th which would review an Auditor report and that the Wage Ordinance discussion could be added to agenda.

### ADJOURNMENT:

**Motion** to Adjourn by C. Juran, seconded by C. McDonough. So voted.

Meeting adjourned at 6:29 PM.

Michael Q. Geary, City Clerk

[Note: Only six pages were provided with this excerpt, labeled pages 1 to 6. Pages 7 to 12 were not included.]

# LEGAL FRAMEWORK

Two distinct legal frameworks govern City employee compensation.

- Union employees: City Manager negotiates under Plan E (MGL c.43); Council funds via appropriation
- Ordinance employees: compensation set by Chapter 56; any change requires a Council vote
- 152 active Ordinance employees govern by the Grid System (grades DH00–DH08, 7 steps each)
- Council has directly voted on every Ordinance COLA in this report period

# COLA HISTORY

Two Council votes set every Ordinance COLA adjustment, FY2023–FY2026.

# ITEM 2 BUDGET STRESSORS

Item 5.4

Budget Stressors and Legislative Relief Strategies

Motion: Councilor Scott, referred 6/16/2026 — draft pending CM sign-off

# FIXED COST PRESSURE

FY2027 non-discretionary costs are outpacing general revenue growth.

Chart: $ Millions (legend: FY2026 Adopted; FY2027 Proposed)

- Pension: $36.9M (FY2026 Adopted); $39.7M (FY2027 Proposed)
- GIC Health: $31.4M (FY2026 Adopted); $33.9M (FY2027 Proposed)
- Debt Service: $20.6M (FY2026 Adopted); $24.0M (FY2027 Proposed)
- Charter / Cherry Sheet: $53.2M (FY2026 Adopted); $56.1M (FY2027 Proposed)

- +$13.5M in growth over FY2026, concentrated in 4 categories
- Together: $153.6M — more than 44% of the General Fund operational budget
- None of these categories are subject to local discretion

## Charter Schools

Net Municipal Charter Cost ($M)

FY23: $24.1M
FY24: $30.7M
FY25: $34.6M
FY26: $41.1M
FY27: $43.4M

+$19.3M net increase, FY23→FY27

Rising assessments and eroding reimbursement compound each year.

- Gross assessment: $52.3M in FY2027, up $26.8M since FY2020
- Reimbursement phases out after 3 years per enrollment cohort
- Ask: permanent reimbursement, enrollment caps, SOA formula reform

## Health Insurance

City-Side GIC Premiums ($M)

FY2026 Adopted: $31.43M
FY2027 Proposed: $33.93M

+$2.5M · +8.0%

GIC premiums are set by the Commonwealth, outside City control.

- System-wide cost (incl. Schools) approaches $60M
- Ask: GIC plan/pharmacy reform, tiering flexibility, Gateway City premium support
- Local: encouraging migration to high-deductible/tiered plans

## Pension System

Pension Assessment ($M)

Legend: City-Side, School-Side

FY2026 Adopted: City $25.78M, School $11.15M, Total $36.93M
FY2027 Proposed: City $27.17M, School $12.49M, Total $39.66M

The pension assessment is actuarially determined — the City has no discretion.

- Governed by MGL c.32 and the LCRS funding schedule
- Ask: PRIT investment enhancements, optional extended amortization
- Ask: State matching program for Gateway City retirement systems
- **FUTURE CONSIDERATION:** Pension Obligation Bonds

## Debt Service

Debt Service ($M)

FY2026 Adopted: $20.58M
FY2027 Proposed: $23.97M

Debt service is FY2027's fastest-growing fixed cost in dollar terms.

- Primary driver: Lowell High School bond amortization
- Ask: higher MSBA reimbursement, a Capital Stabilization Fund
- Ask: an Infrastructure Equity Grant program for Gateway Cities

# ITEM 3 PARKING & CPI

Item 4.11

Parking Garage Fees and Automatic CPI Adjustment
Motion: Councilor McDonough, referred 6/30/2026 — analysis in progress

# PARKING & CPI

Motion 4.11 proposes removing the automatic CPI+1% parking rate adjustment.

- Follows the June 30 Council discussion on the garage rate escalator
- Key issue: the Garage Enterprise Fund relies on the adjustment to track its own cost growth
- Removing it would require an alternate revenue source or a General Fund subsidy
- Full rate/enterprise-fund analysis and peer-city comparison in progress
- Update on status of Audit for prior year COLA
